page: Amazon Web Services m5d.2xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It features an Intel Xeon 8259CL x86_64 processor clocked at 3.1 GHz, configured with 4 physical cores and 8 dedicated vCPUs via simultaneous multithreading. Memory allocation totals 32.0 GB of DDR4 RAM running at 3 GHz, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio. Unlike standard M5 variants, the m5d series incorporates dedicated local hardware storage, specifically a 300 GB NVMe solid-state drive directly attached to the host. Baseline network performance is rated at 2 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations indicate consistent middle-tier performance across multi-threaded and memory-bound operations, offset by modest single-threaded throughput. The processor delivers 6989.22 in stress-ng multi-core testing and 7396.11 on PassMark CPU, while single-core Geekbench (1013.0) and stress-ng (1326.19) scores align with the bottom quartile. Memory bandwidth remains solid at 48.61 GB/s read and 36.16 GB/s write for large un-cached blocks. Application-level metrics reflect stable execution, demonstrating 6.88 million operations per second in Redis SET tests and 6.93 GB/s during static web serving workloads.

The primary architectural tradeoff involves balanced resource allocation paired with high-speed local temporary storage at the expense of peak single-threaded performance or dedicated acceleration. With no hardware GPUs, heavy inference or dense computational modeling is inefficient. The local 300 GB NVMe drive offers high-throughput, low-latency scratch space, making the m5d.2xlarge effective for transient caching tiers, relational database staging, batch data transformation, automated CI/CD builds, and mid-tier backend application hosting.
description: Amazon Web Services m5d.2xlarge is an x86_64 general-purpose instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor and an Intel Xeon 8259CL processor running at 3.1 GHz. Configured with 8 dedicated vCPUs, 32.0 GB of DDR4 memory, and a direct-attached 300 GB NVMe SSD, it delivers a standard 1:4 core-to-memory profile alongside fast local storage. Benchmark testing shows balanced multi-core throughput, including 6.88 million operations per second in Redis and stable PassMark multi-core results, though single-threaded performance remains conservative. The integrated NVMe SSD eliminates network storage bottlenecks for temporary data structures, making the instance well structured for backend web hosting, database read replicas, caching layers, and CI/CD pipelines.
